title: Adoro te, st. 1
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Adoro te devote, latens Deitas,
Quae sub his figuris vere latitas:
Tibi se cor meum totum subiicit,
Quia te contemplans totum deficit.
notes:
English: Godhead here in hiding, whom I do adore, / Masked by these bare shadows, shape and nothing more, / See, Lord, at thy service low lies here a heart / Lost, all lost in wonder at the God thou art.

Latin: Adoro te devote, attributed to St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918). Both public domain. (The English is not yet checked against the printed edition.)

title: Adoro te, st. 2
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Visus, tactus, gustus in te fallitur,
Sed auditu solo tuto creditur.
Credo quidquid dixit Dei Filius:
Nil hoc verbo Veritatis verius.
notes:
English: Seeing, touching, tasting are in thee deceived: / How says trusty hearing? that shall be believed; / What God's Son has told me, take for truth I do; / Truth himself speaks truly or there's nothing true.

Latin: Adoro te devote, attributed to St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918). Both public domain. (The English is not yet checked against the printed edition.)

title: Adoro te, st. 3
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
notes:
English: On the cross thy godhead made no sign to men, / Here thy very manhood steals from human ken: / Both are my confession, both are my belief, / And I pray the prayer of the dying thief.

Latin: Adoro te devote, attributed to St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918). Both public domain. (The English is not yet checked against the printed edition.)

title: Adoro te, st. 4
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
notes:
English: I am not like Thomas, wounds I cannot see, / But can plainly call thee Lord and God as he; / Let me to a deeper faith daily nearer move, / Daily make me harder hope and dearer love.

Latin: Adoro te devote, attributed to St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918). Both public domain. (The English is not yet checked against the printed edition.)

title: Adoro te, st. 5
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
O memoriale mortis Domini!
Panis vivus, vitam praestans homini!
Praesta meae menti de te vivere, Et te illi semper dulce sapere.
notes:
English: O thou our reminder of Christ crucified, / Living Bread, the life of us for whom he died, / Lend this life to me then: feed and feast my mind, / There be thou the sweetness man was meant to find.

Latin: Adoro te devote, attributed to St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918). Both public domain. (The English is not yet checked against the printed edition.)

title: Adoro te, st. 6
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Pie pellicane, Iesu Domine,
Me immundum munda tuo sanguine:
Cuius una stilla salvum facere Totum mundum quit ab omni scelere.
notes:
English: Bring the tender tale true of the Pelican; / Bathe me, Jesu Lord, in what thy bosom ran— / Blood whereof a single drop has power to win / All the world forgiveness of its world of sin.

Latin: Adoro te devote, attributed to St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Poems, ed. Bridges (London, 1918). Both public domain. (The English is not yet checked against the printed edition.)

title: Adoro te, st. 7
source: Adoro te devote (attributed to St Thomas Aquinas)
notes:
English: Jesu, whom I look at shrouded here below, / I beseech thee send me what I thirst for so, / Some day to gaze on thee face to face in light / And be blest for ever with thy glory's sight. Amen.
